saw_lines: Nobody buys a bed on impulse. Buyers compare firmness, price and delivery for weeks before they book a visit.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a buyer decides whether the bed is worth a booking.
Your 10 of 15 ads open on one sleep spa story. Write two or three new openers from your own product and run each one against it.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 2 Nov 2026
points: 10 of 15 copy ads open on one sleep spa line, so one pitch carries the account. None of your 15 ads address price, delivery or returns. Build three openers around those questions and test each against the current one.
One exact copy runs in 7 of 15 ads, so the same words repeat across the account. Keep that copy, but change the opening line and creative in each of the seven so the seven stop sounding identical.

None of your 15 ads carries a proof number, so a new buyer has nothing concrete to weigh before booking. Collect one real figure, such as a review count or orders shipped, and lead the next batch with it.
All 15 ads are video, so there is no still image for placements or visitors who do not play motion. Add still images of the bed in a real bedroom and use them for retargeting and catalog placements.

ads_1: Still bed imagery and new opening angles on price, delivery and returns
soc_1: Brand social strategy for the channels your buyers already use
